objects.definition:
struct ks_struct;
typedef struct ks_struct ks_engine;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for a Keystone engine instance. It represents the assembler context created by ks_open() and must be closed with ks_close(). The underlying structure is not defined in this header, so it is used only as an opaque pointer.

objects.definition:
typedef enum ks_arch {
    KS_ARCH_ARM = 1,    // ARM architecture (including Thumb, Thumb-2)
    KS_ARCH_ARM64,      // ARM-64, also called AArch64
    KS_ARCH_MIPS,       // Mips architecture
    KS_ARCH_X86,        // X86 architecture (including x86 & x86-64)
    KS_ARCH_PPC,        // PowerPC architecture (currently unsupported)
    KS_ARCH_SPARC,      // Sparc architecture
    KS_ARCH_SYSTEMZ,    // SystemZ architecture (S390X)
    KS_ARCH_HEXAGON,    // Hexagon architecture
    KS_ARCH_EVM,        // Ethereum Virtual Machine architecture
    KS_ARCH_RISCV,      // RISC-V architecture
    KS_ARCH_MAX,
} ks_arch;
objects.description: Enumeration of supported target architectures for Keystone. Used with ks_open() and capability queries like ks_arch_supported().
Bitmask enumeration of assembler modes and endianness, combined when calling ks_open() to configure the target’s encoding mode.

objects.definition:
typedef enum ks_err {
    KS_ERR_OK = 0,   // No error: everything was fine
    KS_ERR_NOMEM,      // Out-Of-Memory error: ks_open(), ks_emulate()
    KS_ERR_ARCH,     // Unsupported architecture: ks_open()
    KS_ERR_HANDLE,   // Invalid handle
    KS_ERR_MODE,     // Invalid/unsupported mode: ks_open()
    KS_ERR_VERSION,  // Unsupported version (bindings)
    KS_ERR_OPT_INVALID,  // Unsupported option

    // generic input assembly errors - parser specific
    KS_ERR_ASM_EXPR_TOKEN = KS_ERR_ASM,    // unknown token in expression
    KS_ERR_ASM_DIRECTIVE_VALUE_RANGE,   // literal value out of range for directive
    KS_ERR_ASM_DIRECTIVE_ID,    // expected identifier in directive
    KS_ERR_ASM_DIRECTIVE_TOKEN, // unexpected token in directive
    KS_ERR_ASM_DIRECTIVE_STR,   // expected string in directive
    KS_ERR_ASM_DIRECTIVE_COMMA, // expected comma in directive
    KS_ERR_ASM_DIRECTIVE_RELOC_NAME, // expected relocation name in directive
    KS_ERR_ASM_DIRECTIVE_RELOC_TOKEN, // unexpected token in .reloc directive
    KS_ERR_ASM_DIRECTIVE_FPOINT,    // invalid floating point in directive
    KS_ERR_ASM_DIRECTIVE_UNKNOWN,    // unknown directive
    KS_ERR_ASM_DIRECTIVE_EQU,   // invalid equal directive
    KS_ERR_ASM_DIRECTIVE_INVALID,   // (generic) invalid directive
    KS_ERR_ASM_VARIANT_INVALID, // invalid variant
    KS_ERR_ASM_EXPR_BRACKET,    // brackets expression not supported on this target
    KS_ERR_ASM_SYMBOL_MODIFIER, // unexpected symbol modifier following '@'
    KS_ERR_ASM_SYMBOL_REDEFINED, // invalid symbol redefinition
    KS_ERR_ASM_SYMBOL_MISSING,  // cannot find a symbol
    KS_ERR_ASM_RPAREN,          // expected ')' in parentheses expression
    KS_ERR_ASM_STAT_TOKEN,      // unexpected token at start of statement
    KS_ERR_ASM_UNSUPPORTED,     // unsupported token yet
    KS_ERR_ASM_MACRO_TOKEN,     // unexpected token in macro instantiation
    KS_ERR_ASM_MACRO_PAREN,     // unbalanced parentheses in macro argument
    KS_ERR_ASM_MACRO_EQU,       // expected '=' after formal parameter identifier
    KS_ERR_ASM_MACRO_ARGS,      // too many positional arguments
    KS_ERR_ASM_MACRO_LEVELS_EXCEED, // macros cannot be nested more than 20 levels deep
    KS_ERR_ASM_MACRO_STR,    // invalid macro string
    KS_ERR_ASM_MACRO_INVALID,    // invalid macro (generic error)
    KS_ERR_ASM_ESC_BACKSLASH,   // unexpected backslash at end of escaped string
    KS_ERR_ASM_ESC_OCTAL,       // invalid octal escape sequence  (out of range)
    KS_ERR_ASM_ESC_SEQUENCE,         // invalid escape sequence (unrecognized character)
    KS_ERR_ASM_ESC_STR,         // broken escape string
    KS_ERR_ASM_TOKEN_INVALID,   // invalid token
    KS_ERR_ASM_INSN_UNSUPPORTED,   // this instruction is unsupported in this mode
    KS_ERR_ASM_FIXUP_INVALID,   // invalid fixup
    KS_ERR_ASM_LABEL_INVALID,   // invalid label
    KS_ERR_ASM_FRAGMENT_INVALID,   // invalid fragment

    // generic input assembly errors - architecture specific
    KS_ERR_ASM_INVALIDOPERAND = KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH,
    KS_ERR_ASM_MISSINGFEATURE,
    KS_ERR_ASM_MNEMONICFAIL,
} ks_err;
objects.description: Enumeration of Keystone API and assembler error codes, including generic and architecture-specific assembler errors. Used as return values from functions like ks_open(), ks_option(), ks_errno().

Function pointer type for a user-provided symbol resolver callback. When assembly references an unknown symbol, Keystone may invoke this callback to obtain its value. Return true if resolved and store the value via the out-parameter.
Enumeration of option keys accepted by ks_option(). Controls runtime configuration aspects such as syntax and the symbol resolver.
Enumeration of option values used with ks_option(), primarily to select assembly syntax and formatting behaviors.

Enumeration of AArch64 (ARM64) assembler error codes specific to the Keystone Assembler Engine. Values indicate operand errors, missing required CPU features, or mnemonic parsing failures. The first enumerator is explicitly based on KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH from keystone.h, so its underlying value depends on that header. Intended for reporting/inspecting assembly failures for the ARM64 backend.

Enumeration of ARM-specific assembler error codes for the Keystone engine. Values start at KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH (from keystone.h) and enumerate specific failure reasons: invalid operand, missing required feature, and mnemonic parsing failure. Intended for reporting assembly errors when targeting the ARM architecture. Underlying integral values depend on KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH definition in the included keystone.h.

Error code enumeration for the Keystone EVM (Ethereum Virtual Machine) assembler backend. Values start from KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH (from keystone.h) and enumerate specific EVM assembly errors: invalid operand, missing required feature, and mnemonic parsing failure. Intended for reporting/handling assembler errors for the EVM target.

Enumeration of Hexagon-specific assembler error codes used by the Keystone Assembler Engine. Values start from KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH (defined elsewhere) and enumerate errors such as invalid operands, missing CPU features, and mnemonic parsing failures. Intended for reporting/handling assembly errors for the Hexagon backend. Underlying integral type follows C enum rules; exact numeric values depend on KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH constant from keystone.h.

Enumeration of MIPS-specific assembler error codes in the Keystone Engine. Values map to or follow the base architecture error codes (KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH from keystone.h). Used to report specific failure reasons when assembling MIPS code. Underlying type is implementation-defined enum; use ks_err_asm_mips for type safety.

Enumeration of PowerPC-specific assembler error codes in the Keystone engine. Values start at KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH (from keystone.h) and enumerate PPC-specific failure reasons: invalid operand, missing required ISA/feature, and mnemonic parsing failure. Used to report detailed assembly errors for the PPC backend.

Enumeration of RISC-V specific assembler error codes for the Keystone Assembler Engine. Values start from KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH (defined elsewhere) and enumerate specific failure reasons such as invalid operand, missing ISA feature, or mnemonic parse failure. Used as an error-code type; not a constructible object.

Enumeration of SPARC-specific assembler error codes in the Keystone Assembler Engine. Values start at KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH (from keystone.h) for INVALIDOPERAND, followed by MISSINGFEATURE and MNEMONICFAIL. Intended for reporting assembly errors specific to the SPARC backend. Underlying integral type is unspecified (C enum). Note: exact numeric values depend on KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH definition in the included keystone.h.

Enumeration of SystemZ-specific assembler error codes used by the Keystone Assembler. Values start at KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH (defined in keystone.h) and enumerate specific failure reasons: invalid operand, missing CPU/ISA feature, and mnemonic parsing failure.

Enumeration of x86-specific assembler error codes for the Keystone engine. Values map to architecture-scoped error codes, with INVALIDOPERAND explicitly aligned to KS_ERR_ASM_ARCH from keystone.h. Intended for reporting parsing/assembly failures on x86: invalid operands, missing CPU feature support, or mnemonic parse failure.

functions.name: ks_version
functions.signature: KEYSTONE_EXPORT unsigned int ks_version(unsigned int *major, unsigned int *minor);
functions.description: Return the Keystone API version. Encodes major and minor into the return value as (major << 8) | minor, and optionally writes them to the provided pointers. Use KS_MAKE_VERSION to compare against the return value. If only the combined value is needed, pass NULL for both pointers.
requirements: major may be NULL if the caller does not need the major version.
minor may be NULL if the caller does not need the minor version.
Return value is a combined version (major << 8) | minor.

functions.name: ks_arch_supported
functions.description: Check whether the given architecture (KS_ARCH_*) is supported by the library at runtime. Returns true if supported, false otherwise.
requirements: arch must be a valid ks_arch enumeration value.

functions.name: ks_open
functions.signature: KEYSTONE_EXPORT ks_err ks_open(ks_arch arch, int mode, ks_engine **ks);
functions.description: Create a new Keystone engine instance for the specified architecture and mode. On success, writes the handle to *ks. Use ks_close to release the handle when done.
requirements: arch must be a supported ks_arch value (use ks_arch_supported to check).
mode must be a valid combination of ks_mode flags for the given architecture.
ks must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created handle.
On success, *ks is initialized and must later be closed with ks_close.
On failure, the return value is a ks_err error code; *ks is unspecified and must not be used.

functions.name: ks_close
functions.description: Close and destroy a Keystone engine instance previously created by ks_open. This releases internal resources and cached memory. After return, the handle is invalid and must not be used.
requirements: ks must be a valid handle previously returned by ks_open.
Must be called only when there is no longer any usage of the Keystone handle; calling Keystone APIs after ks_close on the same handle may crash.
Do not reuse the ks handle after this call; it becomes invalid.
Returns KS_ERR_OK on success; other ks_err values indicate failure.

functions.name: ks_errno
functions.description: Report the last error code associated with the given Keystone handle. Similar to errno; the stored error may not be retained after it is read.
requirements: ks must be a valid handle returned by ks_open.
Call after an API failure to retrieve the error code.
Note: like errno, the stored error may not persist after access.

functions.name: ks_strerror
functions.description: Return a human-readable string describing the given ks_err error code. The returned pointer refers to a static/managed string; do not free or modify it.
requirements: code should be a ks_err value.
The returned string pointer must not be freed or modified by the caller.

functions.name: ks_option
functions.signature: KEYSTONE_EXPORT ks_err ks_option(ks_engine *ks, ks_opt_type type, size_t value);
functions.description: Set a runtime option on a Keystone engine. Used to set syntax (KS_OPT_SYNTAX with a ks_opt_value) or register a symbol resolver (KS_OPT_SYM_RESOLVER with a ks_sym_resolver function pointer).
requirements: ks must be a valid handle returned by ks_open.
type must be a valid ks_opt_type (e.g., KS_OPT_SYNTAX, KS_OPT_SYM_RESOLVER).
For KS_OPT_SYNTAX, value must be one of ks_opt_value (e.g., KS_OPT_SYNTAX_INTEL, KS_OPT_SYNTAX_ATT, etc.).
For KS_OPT_SYM_RESOLVER, value must be the address of a ks_sym_resolver callback cast to size_t.
Returns KS_ERR_OK on success; KS_ERR_OPT_INVALID or other ks_err on failure.

functions.name: ks_asm
functions.signature: KEYSTONE_EXPORT int ks_asm(ks_engine *ks, const char *string, uint64_t address, unsigned char **encoding, size_t *encoding_size, size_t *stat_count);
functions.description: Assemble a NULL-terminated assembly string into machine code for the configured architecture/mode. On success, allocates a buffer containing the encoded bytes and returns it via *encoding; the caller must free it with ks_free. Also returns the output size and the number of statements assembled. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; call ks_errno to get the error code.
requirements: ks must be a valid handle returned by ks_open with appropriate arch/mode set.
string must be a NULL-terminated assembly string; use ';' or '\n' to separate statements.
address is the start address for assembly; pass 0 to ignore.
encoding must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated output buffer on success; free it with ks_free.
encoding_size must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the size of the output buffer on success.
stat_count must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of statements successfully processed.
On success, *encoding is dynamically allocated; the caller is responsible for freeing it using ks_free.
On failure (return -1), use ks_errno(ks) to obtain a ks_err error code; do not call ks_free on an uninitialized or untouched *encoding pointer.

functions.name: ks_free
functions.description: Free memory allocated by ks_asm for the output encoding buffer. Call this on the pointer returned via *encoding by ks_asm to avoid memory leaks.
requirements: p must be a pointer previously allocated by ks_asm (the value returned in *encoding).
Do not pass NULL unless allowed by the implementation; behavior is unspecified by this header.
Do not use the memory after it has been freed.

data_types.description: A null-terminated text buffer containing assembly instructions for a target architecture, possibly with multiple statements separated by newlines or semicolons. The content includes mnemonics, operands, registers, immediates, labels, and assembler directives according to the configured architecture/mode and syntax (e.g., Intel, AT&T). May include arbitrary bytes but is expected to parse as assembly text.
